newsitem.title: FRANCE: Source says French govt to take 18bln Ffr from CDC.
newsitem.headline: Source says French govt to take 18bln Ffr from CDC.

text.p: The French government is planning to take 18 billion francs from state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) in its 1997 budget, a source close to the issue said on Thursday.
The source was confirming a report published earlier in the financial daily Les Echos.
The government takes money every year from the bank in return for a state guarantee on deposits if the bank were to collapse. It took 23 billion francs in 1995 and around 21 billion in 1996.
Officials at the bank had no comment while goverment officials were not available for comment.
Goverment sources have said previously it was likely that there would be a transfer from CDC reserves in the 1997 budget, which is due to be presented on September 18.

The source said the total amount planned for next year was in line with a law allowing the government to take up to two percent of deposits on the Livret A savings scheme to cover its guarantee on bank deposits.
